subQuestions.questionText: Chuckle Traders is registered for VAT, although the annual turnover is less than R1 000 000. The standard VAT rate is 15%. The business is owned by Chuckles Berry. Give ONE reason why Chuckles decided to register for VAT.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE valid reason (2 marks; part marks for incomplete/partial responses):
• He will be able to claim VAT input from SARS / He supports or pays VAT for most of his purchases / He wants to benefit from input VAT on certain expenses or assets that he buys.
• He sells goods that are subject to standard rate VAT (15%).
• VAT collections will earn interest for a period of time.
• Should his turnover exceed R1 000 000, he does not have to worry about being penalised by SARS for not complying (compulsory registration).
• He expects his business to grow and will be compelled to register.
• Responsible citizen – collect tax for SARS – improve the economy.
Do NOT accept 'benefit to his cash flow'.

subQuestions.questionText:
Calculate the amount of VAT that is payable to SARS for the two-month period ended 30 April 2022.

VAT-related transactions for the period ended 30 April 2022:

• VAT on drawings of trading stock by Chuckles: R1 200
• VAT on returns from debtors: R2 820
• VAT on discount received from suppliers: R3 360

VAT on sales (output): $87\,400 \times 15/115 = R11\,400$ (1 mark)

VAT Control calculation:
$-2\,600 - 8\,850 + 11\,400 + 1\,200 - 2\,820 + 3\,360$

Mark allocation:
• Balance due by SARS R2 600 (1 mark)
• VAT on purchases R8 850 (1 mark)
• VAT output on sales R11 400 (1 mark) — calculation $87\,400 \times 15/115$
• VAT on drawings R1 200 (1 mark)
• VAT on returns from debtors R2 820 (1 mark)
• VAT on discount received R3 360 (1 mark)
• Correct + or – sign placement on each (operation marks)

Final Answer: R1 690 payable to SARS (one part correct, 9 marks total)

subQuestions.questionText: Chuckles uses the money collected for VAT to pay business expenses. He does not have sufficient cash to make the VAT payments on the due dates. What would you say to Chuckles? State TWO different/separate points.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO valid points (2 marks; could be a comment or advice):

• It is unethical / the money does not belong to the business / agent of SARS.
• He should budget / plan / manage his expenses more effectively.
• Keep detailed records of VAT separate from business records and diarise payment dates.
• Using the money could become a bad habit / rolling of cash.
• He must discontinue this practice.

subQuestions.label: 1.2.2 (a)
subQuestions.questionText: Mani feels that the creditors' clerk is not efficient in performing her duties. Provide evidence to support his opinion. Give ONE point.

subQuestions.label: 2.1.1 (a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Stylish Suits manufactures one type of fashionable men's suit. The financial year ended on 31 March 2022. Calculate the Direct Material Cost for the Production Cost Statement.

Information:
• During the financial year, the business purchased 12 250 metres of fabric for R5 512 500.
• Fabric was issued to the factory to meet the production target of 3 000 suits: 3,2 metres of fabric per suit, with an allowance of 5% thereof for wastage.
subQuestions.memoText:
Direct material cost calculation:

Unit cost per metre: $5\,512\,500 \div 12\,250 = R450$ per metre (1 mark)

Fabric required per suit (with 5% wastage): $3{,}2 \times 105\% = 3{,}36$ metres

Total fabric used: $3\,000 \times 3{,}2 \times 105\% = 10\,080$ metres (2 marks)

Direct Material Cost: $3\,000 \times 3{,}2 \times 105\% \times R450$ (2 marks for application)

OR equivalent: $9\,600 \times 105\% \times 450$ OR $10\,080 \times 450$ OR $3\,000 \times 3{,}36 \times 450$

FINAL ANSWER: R4 536 000 (one part correct, 1 mark)

Alternative method: Closing stock = R976 500, then $5\,512\,500 - (2\,170 \times 450)$ also acceptable.

Total: 6 marks

subQuestions.label: 2.1.1 (b)
subQuestions.questionText:
Calculate the Direct Labour Cost for the Production Cost Statement.

Information on labour:
• 40 Factory machinists, basic monthly salary R9 800 each (involved in production of suits).
• 3 Factory supervisors, basic monthly salary R17 500, total annual bonus R84 000 (recorded as factory overheads).
• Annual bonus distributed between machinists and supervisors in ratio 5:2.
• All employees pay 1% of gross earnings to UIF; employer contributes R-for-R.
subQuestions.memoText:
Direct Labour Cost calculation:

Basic wages: $40 \times R9\,800 \times 12$ months $= R4\,704\,000$ (3 marks)

Bonus payments: Supervisors' bonus = R84 000 (given). Bonus ratio 5:2 (machinists:supervisors).
Machinists' bonus = $R84\,000 \times 5/2 = R210\,000$ (1 mark)

Gross wage: $4\,704\,000 + 210\,000 = R4\,914\,000$ (1 mark)

UIF (employer contribution = 1% of gross): $4\,914\,000 \times 1\% = R49\,140$ (1 mark — if 1% of gross)

FINAL ANSWER: $4\,914\,000 + 49\,140 = R4\,963\,140$ (one part correct)

Total: 6 marks

subQuestions.label: 2.1.1 (c)
subQuestions.questionText:
Calculate the Factory Overhead Cost for the Production Cost Statement.

Information:
• Provisionally calculated FOHC: R941 500
• Adjustments not yet recorded:
  - Invoice of R59 500 for consumable stores not recorded; factory used 60%, office used balance.
  - Rent paid for selling and distribution section: R186 000. Floor space — Factory: 400 m², Selling/distribution: 300 m², Administration: 100 m².
  - Factory insurance R31 500 per month, increased by 8% from 1 January 2022. Premiums for Jan-Mar 2022 not yet paid or recorded.
subQuestions.memoText:
Factory Overhead Cost calculation:

Provisional total: R941 500 (1 mark)

Consumable stores (factory portion 60%): $59\,500 \times 60\% = R35\,700$ (1 mark)

Rent expense for factory: Rent per m² = $186\,000 \div 300 = R620$ per m². Factory rent = $400 \times R620 = R248\,000$ (2 marks)

Insurance (Jan–Mar 2022 with 8% increase): $31\,500 \times 108\% \times 3 = R102\,060$ OR $(31\,500 + 2\,520) \times 3 = R102\,060$ (2 marks)

FINAL ANSWER: $941\,500 + 35\,700 + 248\,000 + 102\,060 = R1\,327\,260$ (one part correct, 1 mark)

Total: 7 marks

subQuestions.questionText:
Complete the Abridged Statement of Comprehensive Income (Income Statement) for the year ended 31 March 2022.

Information:
• 3 000 suits manufactured at unit cost R3 750.
• Total sales R18 104 000.
• Finished goods: 31 March 2022 — R195 000; 31 March 2021 — R260 000.
• Selling and distribution cost (provisional): R866 400.
• Administration costs (provisional): R532 200.
• Adjustments: Consumable stores R59 500 (40% to office); Rent on S&D R186 000; FOHC adjustments as in 2.1.1(c).
subQuestions.memoText:
ABRIDGED STATEMENT OF COMPREHENSIVE INCOME for the year ended 31 March 2022:

Sales: R18 104 000 (given)

Cost of Sales calculation:
Opening stock: R260 000 (1 mark)
Cost of production: $3\,000 \times R3\,750 = R11\,250\,000$ (1 mark) — alternative: per memo 2.1.1 = R10 826 400 method mark
Closing stock: (R195 000) (1 mark)
Cost of Sales: $260\,000 + 11\,250\,000 - 195\,000 = R11\,315\,000$ (one part correct, 1 mark)

Gross Profit: $18\,104\,000 - 11\,315\,000 = R6\,789\,000$ (operation Sales – COS)

Operating Expenses:
• Selling and distribution cost: $866\,400 + 186\,000 = R1\,052\,400$ (2 marks)
• Administration costs: $532\,200 + 23\,800 + 62\,000 = R618\,000$ (3 marks)
  - R23 800 = office portion of consumables ($59\,500 - 35\,700$)
  - R62 000 = administration rent ($100 \times R620$)
Total Operating Expenses: $1\,052\,400 + 618\,000 = R1\,670\,400$ (operation)

Net Profit for the year: $6\,789\,000 - 1\,670\,400 = R5\,118\,600$ (operation GP – OE)

Total: 11 marks

subQuestions.questionText:
Calculate the break-even point for shirts in 2022.

Information (Shirt Factory 2022):
• Selling price per unit: R360,00
• Variable cost per unit: R246,60
• Fixed cost per unit: R94,20
• Units produced and sold: 22 000
subQuestions.memoText:
Break-even point calculation:

Total Fixed Costs: $R94{,}20 \times 22\,000 = R2\,072\,400$ (1 mark — numerator)

Contribution per unit: $R360 - R246{,}60 = R113{,}40$ (2 marks — denominator)

Break-even point: $\dfrac{2\,072\,400}{113{,}40} = 18\,275{,}1$ units

FINAL ANSWER: 18 275,1 units (or 18 276 or 18 275 units) — one part correct (1 mark)

Do NOT accept R, c, or %.
Mark numerator and denominator as such (Principle 11).

Total: 4 marks

subQuestions.questionText:
Fiona has invested in new equipment to make the shoes. She knows that she has saved 10% of the fixed costs for shoes, but she cannot understand why the fixed costs per unit increased. Explain. Provide figures.

Information (Shoe Factory):
• 2022: Fixed cost per unit R117,90; Units produced 15 000
• 2021: Fixed cost per unit R97,80; Units produced 21 200
subQuestions.memoText:
Valid explanation (1 mark) + Figure/s (1 mark):

• Production decreased from 21 200 units to 15 000 units / by 6 200 units / by 29,2% causing fixed cost per unit to increase from R97,80 to R117,90 / by R20,10 / by 20,6% / dis-economies of scale / fixed costs not influenced by the level of production.
• Total fixed costs (FOHC) in 2021 were R1 320 760; reduced to R1 096 500 in 2022 (saving of R224 260 or 16,9% — but this is not the 10% claim, calculation noted).

Although there was a reduction in total fixed costs, the fixed cost per unit increased due to decline in production (by 6 200 units).

Total: 2 marks

subQuestions.questionText:
Identify the variable cost that caused the biggest problem in EACH factory (Shirt, Shoe, Tie). Provide figures. Give a valid solution for EACH problem identified.

Variable cost per unit data (2022 vs 2021):
Shirt: DM 67,90/66,00; DL 136,70/110,00; S&D 42,00/40,50
Shoe: DM 132,40/123,50; DL 105,20/97,20; S&D 44,80/35,50
Tie: DM 48,00/36,30; DL 81,10/80,40; S&D 19,10/21,80
Inflation rate: 6%
subQuestions.memoText:
SHIRT FACTORY (3 marks):
Problem cost: Direct Labour (DLC) (1 mark)
Figure: Increased from R110,00 to R136,70 / by R26,70 / by 24,3% (1 mark)
Solution (any ONE, 1 mark):
• Train (factory) workers to be more efficient
• Improve supervision
• Reduce/control overtime / use casual, cheaper labour after hours
• Set targets for normal time hours (time and motion studies)
• Incentives/bonuses if targets met

SHOE FACTORY (3 marks):
Problem cost: Selling and Distribution (SDC) (1 mark)
Figure: Increased from R35,50 to R44,80 / by R9,30 / by 26,2% (1 mark)
Solution (any ONE, 1 mark):

TIE FACTORY (3 marks):
Problem cost: Direct Material (DMC) (1 mark)
Figure: Increased from R36,30 to R48,00 / by R11,70 / by 32,2% (1 mark)
Solution (any ONE, 1 mark):
• Source cheaper suppliers (without compromising quality)
• Local supplier / reduce transport and storage costs
• Buy in bulk to take advantage of bulk discounts
• Use off cuts (by-products) / minimise wastage
• Train/supervise (factory) workers

Total: 9 marks

subQuestions.questionText:
Complete each of the following sentences by filling in the missing word(s).

subQuestions.questionText:
Calculate the value of closing stock of pots on 28 February 2022.

Information:
• Periodic inventory system; pots valued using weighted-average method.
• Opening stock (1 March 2021): 800 pots, R224 000
• Closing stock (28 February 2022): 980 pots
• Net Purchases: 4 700 pots, R1 712 000 (May: 1 500 @ R320 = R480 000; Sept: 2 300 @ R370 = R851 000; Jan: 1 200 @ R410 = R492 000; Sept Returns: -300 @ -R111 000)
subQuestions.memoText:
Closing stock value calculation (Weighted-average method):

Weighted average unit cost: $\dfrac{224\,000 + 1\,712\,000}{800 + 4\,700} = \dfrac{1\,936\,000}{5\,500} = R352$ per pot

Closing stock value: $352 \times 980 = R344\,960$

Mark allocation:
• Numerator $1\,936\,000$ (224 000 + 1 712 000): 2 marks
• Denominator $5\,500$ (800 + 4 700): 1 mark
• × 980 and final answer: 1 mark (operation, one part correct, must × 980)

FINAL ANSWER: R344 960 (one part correct, 4 marks)

Mark numerator and denominator as such (Principle 11).

subQuestions.label: 3.2.2 (a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Lerato is unsure how long it will take to sell the closing stock of pots. Provide a calculation to address her concern.

Information:
• 4 270 pots sold at R560 each
• Cost of sales: R1 591 040
subQuestions.memoText:
Stock holding period calculation (two acceptable methods):

METHOD 1 — Rand values:
$\dfrac{344\,960}{1\,591\,040} \times 365 = 79{,}1$ days (or 2,6 months)

Mark allocation:
• Numerator R344 960 (see 3.2.1): 1 mark
• Denominator R1 591 040: 1 mark
• × 365 (or × 12) and final answer: 1 mark (one part correct)

METHOD 2 — Units:
$\dfrac{980}{4\,270} \times 365 = 83{,}8$ days (or 2,8 months)

Mark allocation:
• Numerator 980 units: 1 mark
• Denominator 4 270 units: 1 mark
• × 365 and final answer: 1 mark (one part correct)

FINAL ANSWER: 79,1 days / 2,6 months OR 83,8 days / 2,8 months

If Rand amounts are mixed with Units, award 1 mark for the numerator only; no mark on the final answer.

Total: 3 marks

subQuestions.label: 3.2.2 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: Explain whether the period calculated is acceptable, or not.
subQuestions.memoText:
Valid explanation (2 marks; part marks for incomplete/partial responses). Depends on calculation above; figures not necessary.

Possible responses for 'period IS Acceptable':
• Pots are durable items and can be sold in the near future / has a long shelf-life / there is always a need (demand).

Possible responses for 'period is NOT Acceptable':
• Consumers' taste or preference may change / possibility of being replaced by later model, improved products / risk of theft or damage (need to write off) / takes up storage space.

Total: 2 marks
subQuestions.topic: Inventory Valuation - Stock Holding Period Analysis

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the number of pots missing.
subQuestions.memoText:
Missing pots calculation:

Goods available for sale: $800 + 4\,700 = 5\,500$ pots (1 mark)
Pots sold: 4 270 (1 mark)
Closing stock per count: 980 (1 mark — see 3.2.1)

Missing pots: $5\,500 - 4\,270 - 980 = 250$ pots

FINAL ANSWER: 250 pots missing (one part correct, 1 mark)

Total: 4 marks

subQuestions.questionText:
Calculate the value of the closing stock of microwave ovens.

Information (specific identification method):
SWIFT: Opening 380 @ R2 800 = R1 064 000; Purchases 750 @ R2 800 = R2 100 000; Sales 965 @ R4 200 = R4 053 000; Gross profit R1 351 000.
DELTA: Opening 430 @ R3 200 = R1 376 000; Purchases 600 @ R3 200 = R1 920 000; Returns 120 = R384 000; Sales 580 @ R5 600 = R3 248 000; Gross profit R1 392 000.
subQuestions.memoText:
Closing stock of microwave ovens (Specific Identification method):

SWIFT MODEL:
Units remaining: $380 + 750 - 965 = 165$ units (3 marks for the working)
Unit cost: R2 800
Value: $165 \times 2\,800 = R462\,000$ (3 marks)

Alternative: $(1\,064\,000 + 2\,100\,000) - (965 \times 2\,800)$
$= 3\,164\,000 - 2\,702\,000 = R462\,000$

DELTA MODEL:
Units remaining: $430 + 600 - 120 - 580 = 330$ units (3 marks for working)
Unit cost: R3 200
Value: $330 \times 3\,200 = R1\,056\,000$ (3 marks)

Alternative: $(1\,376\,000 + 1\,920\,000 - 384\,000) - (580 \times 3\,200)$
$= 2\,912\,000 - 1\,856\,000 = R1\,056\,000$

TOTAL CLOSING STOCK: $462\,000 + 1\,056\,000 = R1\,518\,000$ (1 mark — one part correct)

Be alert to alternative methods using cost of sales, gross profit or Trading Account format.

Total: 7 marks

subQuestions.questionText: Lerato plans to discontinue selling the Delta model. Give TWO reasons to support this decision and ONE reason against this decision. Quote figures.
subQuestions.memoText:
TWO reasons IN FAVOUR (2 reasons × 2 marks each = 4 marks). Each: explanation (1 mark) + figure (1 mark):
• High returns: possibly poor quality, 120 microwave ovens / 20% of purchases.
• High closing stock / capital tied up in stock: 330 units or R1 056 000 (see 3.2.4).
• Low sales volume: only 580 of 910 (63,7%) / 385 units or R805 000 less than Swift.
• Too expensive for customers: R5 600 selling price (R1 400 more than a Swift model).
• It is a more expensive product: R3 200 cost (pays R400 more than Swift cost).

ONE reason AGAINST (2 marks). Explanation (1 mark) + figure (1 mark):
• Delta stoves generate higher gross profit of R1 392 000 (R41 000 more than Swift); higher mark-up % of 75% (compared to 50% for Swift) / option to reduce selling price R5 600 (R1 400 more than a Swift model).
• Loss of high sales revenue of R3 248 000 may impact cash flow / lose support of a select group of customers (580 units) or reducing the option for clients.

Total: 6 marks

subQuestions.questionText:
The internal auditor discovered that the number of Swift microwave ovens received on 6 January 2022 does not correspond with the number of microwave ovens recorded on the relevant stock card. Identify the problem relating to the Swift microwave ovens on 6 January 2022. Quote figures.

subQuestions.label: 3.2.6 (b)
subQuestions.questionText: State TWO internal control measures that the internal auditor should implement to ensure that such incidents do not occur in the future.

subQuestions.label: 4.1.3 (b)

Calculate the amount of the loan to be paid on 1 July 2022.

• Interest at 14% p.a. on outstanding balance, payable last day of each month
• Interest on loan: June R4 550; July R4 025
subQuestions.memoText:
Loan amount to be paid on 1 July 2022:

METHOD 1 — Difference in interest:

This difference relates to the loan portion repaid.

Loan repaid: $\dfrac{525 \times 12}{0{,}14} = R45\,000$ (one part correct)
